You start Weedtopia again with Rocko and a new profile.


    Your
    previous game state will be preserved as a separate backup file before the restart.
A city. Your team. A new beginning.
Bakers on the way to pick up butter
The machines are still there. What we lacked were honest delivery plans and people who keep their promises.
Between the warm rocks, our next harvest is growing. The old farm is finally getting reliable buyers again.
Let's fill the shelves and trust together again.
Burning Hills has shown what we can achieve together. Now Big Rock City gets its own chance.
All six residents combine their experiences: open books, reliable technology, good food, music and green paths. The new quarry festival belongs to the city and its people.
Big Rock City came together to carry out this project. Everyone involved remains part of the town, with their own stories.
The residents plan and decide together.
Levin opens old files, Berta shows real construction sites and Samira sets up a table for everyone. Together they explain what's missing and what's already working again.
Big Rock City came together to carry out this project. Everyone involved remains part of the town, with their own stories.
The residents plan and decide together.
The books are on the table
Ida finds shady spots, Berta builds the seating areas and Enno sets up the water supply. A former work site becomes a garden that the residents tend to themselves.
Big Rock City came together to carry out this project. Everyone involved remains part of the town, with their own stories.
The community garden at the big rock
The residents plan and decide together.
Rocko: Samira never brought in the chairs outside the café. Repair the town warehouse and café. The government can replace missing starting funds, but we must earn trust ourselves.
Nothing's been happening in the city for a while. A reliable warehouse and our first coffee shop are bringing life back to the streets.
The first meeting spot is set up! Finally, people in the neighborhood can gather again somewhere.
Rocko: Assign teams to the warehouse and café, then sell the first cup. Soon the residents will tell you how they kept the town going through the difficult times.
Do you hear that? People are coming back to the neighborhood. When the warehouse delivers and the shop is stocked, we can finally offer them something.
Our first guests are taken care of. It's nice to see the streets come alive again.
Nia: Assign a warehouse manager and driver. Once the first delivery arrives and the farm runs automatically, we'll open the routes into Copper Lane.
Our team is ready. I'm organizing the warehouse, drivers bring goods further. As soon as the farm runs, we'll turn individual workshops into a real cooperative.
The first delivery has arrived! I'm proud of the drivers. That's how our farm will become a cooperative.
One delivery instead of a speech
Nia: There are still unpaid delivery notes hanging in the warehouse. Repair the building. Then we'll replace empty promises with goods that actually arrive.
I'm Nia. When goods arrive on time, you hardly notice how much planning is behind it. Our warehouse will connect the farm to the city.
The warehouse is ready. Now our goods have a safe place and our team has a shared hub.
Rocko: The mayor has vanished, but the people stayed. Talk to Mila at the farm. We'll start with what is still here.
Hey! I'm Mila. Nice to have you on board. Here the first plants are growing for our new start. I'd be happy to show you how we care for them.
Great to have met you! I think we'll make a great team. Our new start can begin!
Mila: The soil is good; the farm simply stopped working. Repair the first growing plot. A working start means more than another promise.
This place has potential. If we fix it up again, the first harvest will grow here soon. I've already got the seedlings ready.
Hey, our first cultivation plot is thriving again! The seedlings have a home. I'm already looking forward to the first harvest.
Rocko: Collect the market's first daily yield. Supplies now flow reliably. The books remain open, and the residents shape their next chapters themselves.
You've turned the first workshops into a functioning city. I'm proud of our team. Soon you'll be able to choose your own path.
We've made it. The city is standing on its own feet again. Thanks for believing in our team.
A new beginning belongs to all
Mila: Our new helper wants to know where he's needed. Assign him to the field so we can keep working reliably while you visit Burning Hills.
I'll stay here and take care of the cultivation. If you put me in charge, I'll keep the plants in shape while you're taking care of the town.
I've taken over here. The plants are in good hands with me, and you can rely on me.
Rocko: Enno's old machines can do more than stand idle. Repair the butter works, market and bakery so Big Rock City can support itself again.
With the butter factory, supermarket, and bakery, we can close the next big gap. The aroma of fresh bread will draw in the whole city.
The workshops are standing. The bakery alone is already smelling like a good morning for our city.
The industrial district is getting a task
Rocko: Staff the three businesses and send off the first butter and pastries. Everyday life should return to the warm Rock Steps.
Now everything fits together: the factory delivers butter, the baker picks it up and makes something good out of it. That's exactly how I imagined our city.
Our baked goods are a hit with the people! From cultivation to the counter, everyone is now contributing their part.
From the old quarry to the table
Mila: This harvest belongs to the town, not a locked safe. Collect the first crate; after that, someone will help you permanently in the field.
The buds are ripe! I love this moment. Let's bring them in, then the next plants will have space.
The first harvest is safely stored away. Well done! You have a knack for plants.
Jaro: The processing facility was never fully set up. Talk to me and repair it. We'll get the old equipment working again.
Jaro is the name. These machines have seen better days, but we'll get them running again. We're refining Mila's harvest here into high-quality buds.
The machines are running again! I knew we could get this workshop up and running together.
Jaro: A repaired facility isn't enough. Give the processing team a permanent workplace and a routine the drivers can rely on.
The workshop is running again! I'll take over processing. Regular harvests and a free buffer are all I need for a good workday.
Everything's set up. I'm keeping the processing going – our team will get reliable good stuff.
Rocko: Berta wants real neighbourhoods, not a backdrop for the next election. Choose at least one house and one park on the building plots, then develop them.
A city is more than its workshops. People need a home and a green space to breathe. I'm especially looking forward to that.
The first new homes and park are here. I can already imagine how the neighbors will live together here.
Rocko: Collect the first daily yields, staff the house and park, and complete one resident assignment from the daily tasks. Then we'll head to the works district together.
Our neighborhood is coming alive. Our neighbors support us with daily bonuses, and new connections are forming in the park. Let's take good care of them.
Our neighbors are helping us, and we're helping them. It finally feels like a community again.
The city is counting its people
Rocko: No one sits behind closed doors at the town hall now. Visit it and recruit a team member. Everyone should be able to see the new decisions.
We need more helping hands. In the team, you can get to know someone with a Worker card. I'll take care of making sure everyone finds their right spot.
Our team is growing. New faces, new ideas – that's exactly what the city needs now.
The town hall without secret doors

Berta has built the first houses on the rock with Rocko. Since the mayor disappeared, she's holding the construction sites together with a pencil and a lot of patience. She only believes promises when someone helps out.
Berta spreads out a worn-out building plan. Under the beautiful facades, simple things are missing: storage spaces, tools and a reliable work path. Help her finish the first building blocks for real.
Berta: We're one step further. Here's something we've accomplished together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Berta notices that the city is working together again.
A plan with ears of donkey
Berta tells the story of her mother, who waited for her every evening on the unfinished promenade. She wants to create a place where workers can sit after their shift.
Berta: We're one step further. Here's something we've accomplished together.
The Sunset Bank at the Rock
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Berta notices that the city is working together again.
An old model house stands alone in Berta's notebook on an empty space. Today she'd rather build a quarter where people meet. Decide what forms its center.
Berta: We're one step further. Here's something we've accomplished together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Berta notices that the city is working together again.
An open workshop gives ideas a fixed place. Berta wants to pass on the experiences to the next helpers.
Berta finds her first apprentice's letter again. For the first time, she doesn't have to fix every mistake herself. Together you can pass on responsibility to the next generation.
Berta: We're one step further. Here's something we've accomplished together.

Enno pulls out a dusty box, revealing a small booster motor inside. He wants to test it in everyday life before someone makes big promises about it again.
Enno: We're one step further. Something stays that we've achieved together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Enno notices that the city is working together again.
Each workshop holds the same rare parts back. Enno suggests a shared shelf. Reliable supply chains show that sharing can strengthen operations.

Ida grew on the edge of the quarry. She knows the plants that survive in every crevice. When the development plans disappeared, a torn landscape remained. She wants to show that a growing city doesn't have to give up its surroundings.
Ida leads you to an unassuming plant in the warm rock. She wants to turn a forgotten corner into an accessible garden. Build your first meeting point and help with supply.
Ida: We're one step closer. There's something we've accomplished together that stays here.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Ida notices that the city is working together again.
The old quarry path is too arduous for many residents. Ida plans short stages with seating and shade. The new quarter should be part of it from the start.
Ida: We're one step closer. There's something we've accomplished together that stays here.
Resting places on the rock path
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Ida notices that the city is working together again.

Levin was responsible for the city treasury, but never got to see the crucial books. Empty folders remained and his bad reputation. He wants to reveal what happened without making people pay for someone else's theft.
Levin opens the old treasure chest: inside, there's only a theater program and unpaid delivery notes. A first proper delivery gives him a verifiable start for the new ledger.
We're one step further. Something remains that we've achieved together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Levin notices that the city is working together again.
Behind a crumpled delivery note is a bakery that never received its pay. Levin collects the names of those affected and wants to see that supply comes back.
We're one step further. Something remains that we've achieved together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Levin notices that the city is working together again.
Levin has found out how fake invoices made the starting capital disappear. He wants to publicly explain the documents. Help him show the new trade routes as a comprehensible counterexample.
We're one step further. Something remains that we've achieved together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Levin notices that the city is working together again.

Levin closes the last page of the old book. The new one doesn't start with a large credit, but with a resolution by the residents: From now on, decisions will be explained collectively.
We're one step further. Something remains that we've achieved together.

Lotte used to play at Big Rock City's quarry festival. After the mayor disappeared, the stage and instrument case remained closed. She wants to bring back the festival, but this time the residents should decide for themselves.
Under a dusty plane, Lotte finds her old stage. Before she announces a big festival, she wants to give the people who stayed here a small performance.
Lotte: We're one step further. Something remains that we've achieved together.
Lotte's first performance after the silence
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Lotte notices that the city is working together again.
Lotte hears more voices than instruments when setting up. A neighborhood chorus could turn the festival into a shared story. Take care of its first rehearsal.
Lotte: We're one step further. Something remains that we've achieved together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Lotte notices that the city is working together again.
One agency offers Lotte a big concert. She remembers a party where everyone brought their own chair. Decide which symbol sets the open stage.
Lotte: We're one step further. Something remains that we've achieved together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Lotte notices that the city is working together again.
An open workshop gives ideas a fixed place. Lotte wants to pass on the experiences to the next helpers.
The rock wall now carries the sound into the new streets. Lotte leaves the last performance to young musicians and listens for the first time from the audience.
Lotte: We're one step further. Something remains that we've achieved together.

Samira's grandfather opened the café at the old quarry. When city hall collapsed, she still set out chairs every morning. For her, a new beginning starts with a warm cup and an empty seat.
Samira shows you the empty spot in front of her café. She wants reliable guests, not a fancy photo shoot. Get the first small round going.
Samira: We're one step further. There's something we've accomplished together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Samira notices that the city is working together again.
On an old postcard, Samira discovers her grandfather's baking recipe. She barely remembers his voice, but still recalls the scent. The bakery can make something new out of it.
Samira: We're one step further. There's something we've accomplished together.
The recipe card from the Rocko's Café
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Samira notices that the city is working together again.
The neighbors know Samira's orders, but not her name. She plans a long table. You decide whether stories or shared dinner will open the evening.
Samira: We're one step further. There's something we've accomplished together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Samira notices that the city is working together again.
A workshop gives ideas a fixed place. Samira wants to pass on her experiences to the next team members.
A table for the whole street
Samira has opened up alone every morning. Now a former regular customer wants to join the café with her. Help them make the business reliable enough for a free afternoon.
Samira: We're one step further. There's something we've accomplished together.
The neighbors take over part of the planning. Samira notices that the city is working together again.
Sit down. The city isn't running away from us.
Samira: The city is growing again. Will you help me with a new round for the people who now live here?

Shared purse and collection. Buildings, delivery routes, and stories belong to each city. Both taken cities will also continue working during your trip.

The mayor of Big Rock City has run off with the starting funds. The government has asked us to take over this town too, after everything we've achieved in Burning Hills.

The people there have stayed. Together, we'll get deliveries moving again, open the books and give the town its future back.
I'll pick up the butter with my delivery truck directly from the butter factory. Back in my bakery, I bake and sell pastries made from it. During the trip, the bakery is closed.
Welcome to our Coffee Cooperative! As soon as the city warehouse delivers, we'll take care of sales. A suitable manager keeps the store running reliably.
I'll start when goods and space are ready at the destination. Additional drivers and expanded warehouses keep the cooperative in motion.
This is where our new neighbourhood will grow. Homes bring residents and worker cards; parks bring new VIP assignments. Let's build both and bring Burning Hills to life.
An empty conveyor belt doesn't help anyone. I'll process the harvest as long as there's space in the buffer zone. If things are stuck here, check out the warehouse and its drivers.
The next harvest is already growing. Pick the buds in time, then there's room for fresh plants. With a manager, cultivation will keep going while you explore the city.
Good logistics takes teamwork. I keep the warehouse running, and our drivers bring the goods into town. Each open driver slot is a new connection for Burning Hills.
Look around: every repaired workshop is a fresh start. I keep track of things at the town hall, while you bring Burning Hills back to life.

Our Meeting Point is Coffee Shop 2: Stage 5 and a installed Pipeline. This includes 360 sold buds since the start of this section.
Our Neighbors are Celebrating! A House and a Park on Level 5 are enough. Existing buildings count; new plots aren't needed.
Activate the town warehouse and the first coffee shop. Rocko is waiting for you at the town hall.
Nothing's been happening in the city for a while. A reliable warehouse and our first coffee shop are bringing life back to the streets.
The first meeting spot is set up! Finally, people in the neighborhood can gather again somewhere.
Assign a town warehouse manager, delivery driver and coffee shop manager. Sell at least one refined bud.
Do you hear that? People are coming back to the neighborhood. When the warehouse delivers and the shop is stocked, we can finally offer them something.
Our first guests are taken care of. It's nice to see the streets come alive again.
Assign a manager and driver to the farm warehouse. An actual delivery must reach the town dock.
Our team is ready. I'm organizing the warehouse, drivers bring goods further. As soon as the farm runs, we'll turn individual workshops into a real cooperative.
The first delivery has arrived! I'm proud of the drivers. That's how our farm will become a cooperative.
Talk to Nia. Repair the farm warehouse. Its first visual tier has one driver slot.
I'm Nia. When goods arrive on time, you hardly notice how much planning is behind it. Our warehouse will connect the farm to the city.
The warehouse is ready. Now our goods have a safe place and our team has a shared hub.
Talk to Mila at the first growing plot. We'll start small.
Hey! I'm Mila. Nice to have you on board. Here the first plants are growing for our new start. I'd be happy to show you how we care for them.
Great to have met you! I think we'll make a great team. Our new start can begin!
